english: "Shepherd, are your sheep good?" "They are good and strong, stranger. This ram is strong. The wool is thick. Sit down and look at them." "I am looking." "I seek wool." "What do you give?" "I have no gold. I give two he-goats." "Two he-goats?" "Two he-goats and two lambs!" "Three lambs." "Four lambs!" "I give three." "Let it be so, and take the wool." "May the gods protect you." Then he bound the wool with a cord and carried the load. The dog followed him. He was sweating. He sat down under the hazel by the marsh. A crane was standing there. Then he rose, went on, and made a hymn of praise.

english: "Shepherd, I am king. Hear me, and give me wool and a ram." "King, I hear you. I give you wool and a ram. Lambs I do not give; I protect them with my dog." "Who guards you?" "The dog guards me." "Take gold." "Gold I do not eat. Give me the field." "The field is broad and good. I will give it to you. Let us set a pledge. Dyeus is witness. If one deceives the other, may Perkunos kill him." "Carry the wool and the ram to the village." "I will carry them." Then the king's troops arrived and carried the ram away. He stood at the door and looked at the field. The king spoke to the queen: "He is a knower." The queen said: "May the goddess protect him."
